advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the sync commands fail-closed: capture the SSM value into a variable, assert `aws` exit status and a non-empty result before invoking `gh secret set` (or document `set -o pipefail` + a non-empty guard), so a failed fetch cannot silently blank the mirror.
evidence: infra/runbooks/ssm-secret-write-only.md:97 'Keep shell tracing off, do not echo the values' — removes the operator's ability to notice a bad fetch
ABSENCE: no `set -o pipefail`, no exit-status / non-empty capture check before the value reaches `gh secret set`, so a failed producer (aws) yields a 'success' verdict
advisory.finding: The sync one-liners pipe `aws ssm get-parameter ... | gh secret set`; with no `set -o pipefail`, if the aws fetch fails (wrong name, missing kms:Decrypt, expired creds) the pipeline still runs `gh secret set` on empty/partial stdin and exits 0, silently overwriting the GitHub mirror with an EMPTY or garbage value. Because the runbook tells operators to keep shell tracing off and not echo values, a failed fetch is indistinguishable from a successful sync.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use a guarded two-step form, e.g. `v=$(aws ssm get-parameter --with-decryption --name /rebar/prod/anthropic-api-key --query 'Parameter.Value' --output text) && [ -n "$v" ] && printf '%s' "$v" | gh secret set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY --repo navapbc/rebar` (with `set -euo pipefail`).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify/adjust the GERRIT_SSH_PRIVKEY sync so the multi-line private key round-trips byte-exact (avoid `--output text` mangling), consistent with the file-redirect form in g2p-ci-credentials.md §2d.
evidence: infra/runbooks/ssm-secret-write-only.md:109-111 `aws ssm get-parameter --with-decryption --name /rebar/prod/ci-gerrit-ssh-key ... --output text | gh secret set GERRIT_SSH_PRIVKEY --repo navapbc/rebar`
infra/runbooks/g2p-ci-credentials.md:105 `gh secret set GERRIT_SSH_PRIVKEY --repo navapbc/rebar < ~/.ssh/rebar_ci_gerrit` — the established form uses a file redirect, not `--output text`

infra/runbooks/g2p-ci-credentials.md:12 'CI service account **SSH private key** ... SSM `/rebar/prod/ci-gerrit-ssh-key` + GitHub Actions secret `GERRIT_SSH_PRIVKEY`' confirms this row is a multi-line private key
advisory.finding: GERRIT_SSH_PRIVKEY is a multi-line private key, but the command syncs it via `--query 'Parameter.Value' --output text` piped to `gh secret set`. `--output text` does not reliably preserve a multi-line value's trailing newline/formatting, and the sibling runbook's own working command sets this exact secret via a file redirect (`gh secret set GERRIT_SSH_PRIVKEY ... < ~/.ssh/rebar_ci_gerrit`), not `--output text`. A key synced this way can lose its final newline and break SSH auth in the Verified-vote workflow.
advisory.suggested_fix: For the SSH-key row, avoid `--output text`; write to a temp file or use a form that preserves newlines exactly before `gh secret set` (matching g2p-ci-credentials.md §2d).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the optional manual timestamp drift check meets AC-3's 'operation-linked/in-process fallback' intent, or explicitly record that it was evaluated and left manual-only.
evidence: infra/runbooks/ssm-secret-write-only.md:121-124 'Optional drift check ... compare ... timestamp freshness check only; if a mirror is older than its SSM source, rerun the sync command above.'

ticket f116-c8d0-1e69-4361 AC: 'Optional (evaluate): a drift check ... surfaced through an existing operational channel (no new CI-provider-only mechanism; must have an operation-linked or in-process fallback per project.portability).'
advisory.finding: AC item 3 asks the drift check to be 'surfaced through an existing operational channel ... must have an operation-linked or in-process fallback', but the runbook provides only a manual `gh secret list --json name,updatedAt` vs LastModifiedDate eyeball comparison with no operational-channel hook. It is written as 'Optional', which the ticket permits, but reviewers should confirm the optional-manual form satisfies the stated portability requirement.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert each SSM source is piped into its CORRECT mirror (e.g. match the full multi-line 'aws ssm get-parameter --name <path> ... | gh secret set <NAME>' block per row) rather than the source and target substrings independently.
evidence: expected_commands contains separate entries 'aws ssm get-parameter --with-decryption --name /rebar/prod/anthropic-api-key' and 'gh secret set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY --repo navapbc/rebar' (test_secret_rotation_runbook.py:23-24), each asserted only via 'assert command in text' (line 34)

Named violating input: editing the runbook so line 101 keeps '--name /rebar/prod/anthropic-api-key' while its piped line 103 becomes 'gh secret set JIRA_API_TOKEN --repo navapbc/rebar' leaves all eight asserted substrings present — both tests still pass despite the mirror now receiving the wrong secret.
The sync block (infra/runbooks/ssm-secret-write-only.md:100-116) is entirely added by this diff, so the source->mirror pipe mapping is newly introduced behavior.
advisory.finding: The sync-command test asserts each 'aws ssm get-parameter ... <SSM path>' fragment and each 'gh secret set <NAME>' fragment as INDEPENDENT substrings, never that a given SSM source is piped into its matching mirror. A cross-wired pipeline (an SSM source's value piped into the wrong 'gh secret set' target) would keep every asserted substring present and the test green, so the test cannot detect a miswire in the exact source->mirror mapping the runbook introduces.
scenarios: A future edit to the runbook accidentally pipes one SSM parameter's value into a different GitHub mirror's 'gh secret set' target.
advisory.suggested_fix: Assert on the contiguous pipeline per row, e.g. build expected as tuples of (ssm_path, secret_name) and assert a regex like rf"--name {re.escape(path)}[\s\S]*?\| gh secret set {re.escape(name)} --repo navapbc/rebar" matches, so a source->mirror miswire fails the test.
